source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
In Cambodia, corn harvesting is almost entirely done by hand, which requires significant labor: both cutting the stalk and picking the ear. Harvest requires suitable timing/labor scheduling so the field can be cleared efficiently, and this can vary somewhat by field, since practices differ from farmer to farmer. Following common practice: farmers typically break the ear off the stalk, then remove/husk the ear and place ears together into a pile, in order to allow the husks to dry out, and this material can also be used as compost material afterward.

Crop debris left over after harvest can be beneficial by being used as compost, or as animal feed; if not managed and left to decompose in the field, it can become a source of disease inoculum for the next crop cycle -- so residue should ideally be gathered and composted properly.
